draft.editorial_deck: Officials and industry speakers discuss computing facilities, skills and rules for public services.
draft.what_happened: Hong Kong’s international computer conference opened with discussion of artificial intelligence and the city’s development plans. Innovation minister Sun Dong described investment in research and computing facilities, support for businesses and efforts to improve local skills.
draft.why_it_matters: The plans link wider use of the technology with safety and responsibility. Selected government departments will test requirements for bidders on public-facing AI service projects to declare compliance with safety and ethical standards.
draft.for_humans: Skills programs and business support are intended to help people and smaller firms adopt artificial intelligence.
draft.for_ai: Selected public-service projects will require bidders to declare compliance with safety and ethical standards.
body_paragraphs: Sun said the government would support smaller firms through a digital transformation program and develop talent through a public skills initiative. He also described plans for industry management frameworks and safety guidance.

Conference participants discussed how people and AI could work together and how organizations could protect systems and data. Industry speakers stressed that technology must address actual needs to create value.
draft.limitation: The article reports conference discussion and government plans, including requirements limited to selected departments.
